concepts.title: Rectangle and Its Diagonals
concepts.definition: A rectangle is a quadrilateral whose angles are all right angles and whose opposite sides are equal; equivalently, its two diagonals must be of equal length, must cut each other at their midpoints, and can cross at any angle - which is exactly what the carpenter must arrange with her two strips.
concepts.formula: rectangle: all angles 90 degrees, opposite sides equal, diagonals equal and bisecting
concepts.key_idea: Equal strips joined at their midpoints with endpoints threaded into a four-sided frame force a rectangle.

solution_steps.explain: All four angles must be right angles for the figure to qualify as a rectangle.
Opposite sides must be equal in length.
The diagonals must be equal and must bisect each other; the carpenter satisfies this by taking equal strips joined at their midpoints.

concepts.title: Angle Sum of a Quadrilateral
concepts.definition: Drawing one diagonal splits any quadrilateral into two triangles, and since each triangle contributes 180 degrees, the four angles of every quadrilateral total 360 degrees; this is why three right angles force the fourth to be a right angle too.
concepts.key_idea: Two triangles glued along a diagonal hand over 180 + 180 = 360 degrees.

solution_steps.explain: Sum the given angles of the quadrilateral.
The full angle sum is 360 degrees, so the fourth angle is what remains.

concepts.title: Parallelogram
concepts.definition: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral whose opposite sides are parallel; it arises by drawing two pairs of parallel lines that do not meet at right angles, and rectangles are the special parallelograms with right angles.
concepts.formula: parallelogram: opposite sides parallel and equal, opposite angles equal
concepts.key_idea: Parallel opposite sides are the defining feature; right angles upgrade it to a rectangle.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp104.txt lines 689-740 (more quadrilaterals with parallel opposite sides)

solution_steps.explain: Mark the opposite sides and confirm each pair runs parallel.
If the crossing is not at right angles the figure is a parallelogram but not a rectangle.
Opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal in every parallelogram.

concepts.title: Rhombus and Its Angles
concepts.definition: A quadrilateral with all four sides of the same length is a rhombus; a diagonal of a rhombus makes four equal angles, and opposite angles of the rhombus are equal - for instance a rhombus built with one angle of 50 degrees has angles 50, 130, 50 and 130.
concepts.key_idea: Equal sides force equal diagonal angles, and the diagonal splits the vertex angle into equal halves.

concepts.title: Kite
concepts.definition: A kite is a quadrilateral whose adjacent side pairs are equal, labellable as AB = BC and CD = DA; its diagonal joining the unequal-vertex pair bisects the two angles it meets and also bisects the other diagonal perpendicularly, which follows from triangle congruences.
concepts.formula: kite: AB = BC and CD = DA (adjacent equal pairs)
concepts.key_idea: Two congruent triangles glued along a shared side give the kite its symmetric diagonal behaviour.

solution_steps.explain: Check AB = BC and CD = DA to confirm the figure is a kite.

solution_steps.action: use triangle congruence on the halves
solution_steps.explain: Triangles AOB and COB are congruent, giving AO = OC and the right angle at O.
The same congruence shows the shared diagonal bisects the angles at B and D.

concepts.title: Trapezium and Co-interior Angles
concepts.definition: A trapezium is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel opposite sides; angles on the same leg between the parallels add to 180 degrees, and when the non-parallel sides are equal the figure is an isosceles trapezium whose base angles match.
concepts.key_idea: Parallel sides force the two angles along each leg to be supplementary.

solution_steps.explain: The two angles on one leg between the parallel sides are co-interior.
